identity.focus_intro: These projects explore three connected engineering problems. Each one links to the implementation so you can inspect the decisions, boundaries and code.
identity.focus_title: A clearer path from code to delivery.
identity.headline: Software. Infrastructure. Connected.
identity.intro: From a working application to a repeatable delivery path. Explore my public engineering lab across interfaces, networks and services.
identity.name: Jenya

projects.boundary: Desired-state definitions in an engineering lab; no running cluster is implied.
projects.description: Argo CD and Kustomize definitions connect applications, networking and observability. Separate development and smoke roots make the intended environments readable in Git.

evidence_explanations.README.md: CI-supported dev and smoke roots, local render commands and unsupported environment boundaries.
evidence_explanations.clusters/dev/kustomization.yaml: Argo CD app composition for namespaces, dev networking, Loki, Grafana, Vector, image updater and tenants.
evidence_explanations.clusters/smoke/kustomization.yaml: Reduced FastAPI, CrewAI and Jaeger desired state for disposable acceptance checks.
evidence_explanations.docs/architecture.md: Reconciliation model, ownership split from provisioning, required secrets and non-live evidence boundary.
evidence_explanations.scripts/validate_opa_manifests.py: Evaluates each rendered Kubernetes resource against OPA policies and rejects reported violations.
evidence_explanations.tests/test_dev_contract.sh: Offline render assertions for tenants, pinned components, OTLP routing and excluded platform resources.

projects.evidence_summary: Follow a Git change into two Kustomize environment roots: dev composes networking, observability and tenants; smoke keeps a smaller acceptance stack.
projects.focus_detail: Express the desired environment in Git, with explicit application and platform boundaries.
projects.problem: How do application and platform changes share one reviewable delivery path?
projects.title: Deployment, made explicit.
projects.verification_note: Render both roots, run contract tests and evaluate the rendered manifests with OPA as described in the README. These checks do not verify a running cluster, DNS, certificates or telemetry delivery.

projects.boundary: Provisioning code and workflows; no currently running environment or billing guarantee is claimed.
projects.description: Terraform provisioning and Argo CD bootstrap describe the route from cloud resources to application delivery. Bounded smoke and cleanup workflows make the lifecycle explicit.

evidence_explanations..github/workflows/timeweb-smoke.yaml: Opt-in cloud smoke: provision, bootstrap, reconcile, check applications and destroy unless explicitly retained.
evidence_explanations.README.md: Operator prerequisites, workflow purposes, local validation and cleanup boundaries.
evidence_explanations.Taskfile.yaml: Side-effect-labelled plan, bootstrap, apply, status and destroy commands with revision guard.
evidence_explanations.docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: Infrastructure versus GitOps ownership, root selection, recovery flow and evidence limitations.
evidence_explanations.terraform/timeweb/main.tf: Master and worker preset lookups, estimated run-cost precondition and versioned cluster module.
evidence_explanations.tests/test_ephemeral_smoke.sh: Offline assertions for cost guard, versioned roots, secret handling, smoke checks and cleanup contract.

projects.evidence_summary: Trace an optional Timeweb cluster from preset selection and estimated-cost guard through Argo CD bootstrap, application smoke checks and default teardown.
projects.focus_detail: Keep provisioning, bootstrap and cleanup steps visible instead of relying on undocumented setup.
projects.problem: How do you make environment setup easier to repeat and inspect?
projects.title: Infrastructure, repeatable.
projects.verification_note: Use the README offline validation commands; do not dispatch cloud workflows or run Terraform apply/destroy to review this copy. A cost estimate is not a billing guarantee, and no live cluster is claimed.

projects.boundary: Application code in an engineering lab; no hosted commercial service or customer results are claimed.
projects.description: The app-poly-gitops lab includes a standalone browser UI for projects and chat alongside this FastAPI service for project conversations, stored transcripts and telemetry. GitOps delivery is defined in the related infrastructure repositories.
projects.focus_detail: Connect API behavior, conversation persistence and telemetry in one inspectable backend.
projects.problem: How do browser interactions connect to chat APIs and application state?
projects.title: AI chat, from UI to API.
